cases.answer: Tank level alarms (measured by LT tags) get a default delay of 30 s for H and L limits [alarm-philosophy §Delay times p.2]. cases.question: Why is the delay for the high exhaust gas temperature alarm 10 s and not 5 s?
retrieved: alarm-philosophy / Exhaust gas temperature delay p.2 cos=0.889
alarm-philosophy / Delay times p.2 cos=0.814
cause-and-effect / Main engine protection p.1 cos=0.807
alarm-philosophy / Priorities and alarm groups p.1 cos=0.762
alarm-philosophy / Purpose and principles p.1 cos=0.752
alarm-philosophy / Limit levels and hysteresis p.1 cos=0.716
cited: alarm-philosophy / Exhaust gas temperature delay p.2
cases.answer: The delay is 10 s and not 5 s for three reasons. First, thermocouple lag: sheathed Type K thermocouples in a thermowell have a time constant of about 4 to 6 s, so a 10 s delay (about two time constants) is needed to confirm the temperature is above the limit and ignore short excursions. Second, nuisance alarms during load changes: load changes over 10 % within a minute cause temperature overshoots of 10 to 15 degrees C for roughly 5 to 8 s, and a 10 s delay prevents nuisance alarms during manoeuvring. Third, the extra wait costs no protection, as damage develops over minutes and the H alarm is an early warning, while the real protection is the HH limit with a 2 s delay. [alarm-philosophy §Exhaust gas temperature delay p.2]
